title: AVAir 3378
summary: AVAir Flight 3378, a Fairchild Swearingen Metroliner turboprop, departed Raleigh-Durham at 21:25 and climbed to only 300 feet before encountering problems. The aircraft maintained appropriate climb speed but executed an excessive rate of turn instead of the standard 22 degrees, causing the aircraft to descend. The aircraft struck water in a reservoir and continued onto land.
probable_cause: The failure of flight crew to maintain a proper flightpath. Contributing factors were the ineffective management and supervision of flight crew training and operations and inappropriate FAA surveillance.

factors.evidence: Weather at the time included low ceiling and low visibility
Improper instrument scanning by the first officer
Lack of company response to documented indications of difficulties in the first officer's piloting
Aircraft maintained excessive rate of turn causing the plane to descend and strike water in reservoir

events.text: Aircraft took off from Raleigh-Durham International Airport
Aircraft climbed to 300 feet maintaining appropriate climb speed
Aircraft executed excessive rate of turn of 40 to 45 degrees
Aircraft descended and struck water in reservoir 100 feet from shoreline then continued onto land into forest
